workflow.inline_plan_threshold.description: Plans with this many tasks or fewer are executed inline by the orchestrator instead of spawning a separate subagent, which avoids the token overhead of launching an agent for a tiny job. Set it to 0 to always spawn subagents, or raise it to inline more small plans. The default of two keeps very cheap plans fast.

workflow.max_discuss_passes.description: Limits how many rounds of questions GSD will go through in the discuss phase before it stops and moves on. A higher number allows a deeper, more thorough exploration of the phase, while a lower number keeps the discussion short. The default of three is usually enough to surface the key issues without fatigue.

workflow.mvp_mode.description: Persists the MVP flag in config so every phase is framed as a vertical slice one user-visible capability at a time (UI, then API, then database) without needing the --mvp flag on each CLI command. When on, the planner, executor, verifier, and discovery surfaces all treat phases this way. Use it when your whole milestone is structured as thin end-to-end slices.

workflow.node_repair.description: Lets GSD automatically retry and fix a failed plan task (a node) before reporting the failure to you. When on, the executor diagnoses the failure and attempts corrective edits, which can save you from stepping in on routine compilation errors, test flakiness, or small logic mistakes. Turn it off if you want to inspect and fix every failure yourself.

workflow.node_repair_budget.description: Sets how many times GSD may automatically retry a single failed task before it gives up and escalates the failure to you. A higher budget can recover from flaky or multi-step problems, but it also means a truly stuck task will waste more time before you see it. The default of two strikes a balance between resilience and quick escalation.

workflow.nyquist_validation.description: Enables Nyquist-inspired validation coverage auditing during the workflow. When on, GSD analyzes your tests and requirements to estimate how well they sample the possible behaviors of the code, and flags areas where coverage is too sparse to give confidence. Turn it off if the coverage-audit noise outweighs its value for a fast-moving project.

workflow.pattern_mapper.description: Runs a pattern mapper step before planning when research or other context is available. The pattern mapper looks across your codebase and project signals to surface recurring patterns, conventions, and anti-patterns that the planner should respect, so new work fits the existing design rather than contradicting it.

workflow.plan_bounce.description: Enables an external plan-bounce validation step against each generated PLAN.md. When on, every plan is passed through the command set in `workflow.plan_bounce_script`, and a non-zero exit code blocks the workflow from proceeding. This lets you enforce custom structural or policy rules on plans (required sections, estimation limits, banned approaches) before execution begins.

workflow.plan_bounce_passes.description: How many iterative plan-bounce passes GSD runs against a plan. Each pass re-validates the (possibly revised) plan through the bounce script, so a value greater than 1 lets a plan be reworked and re-checked up to this many times before it is finally rejected. Use a higher value when your script produces fixable findings and you want GSD to attempt corrections first.

workflow.plan_bounce_script.description: Path to the executable script used for plan-bounce validation when `workflow.plan_bounce` is enabled. GSD runs this script with the path of the PLAN.md file as its first argument and pipes the plan content over stdin; the script must exit 0 for the plan to pass. Set it to null (the default) when you are not using plan-bounce validation.

workflow.plan_check.description: Enables a dedicated checker agent that reviews a finished plan for correctness, consistency, and completeness before execution begins. When on, the plan gets a second pair of eyes that can catch missing steps, contradictions, or unsafe approaches. Leave this on for confidence, or turn it off to shave a little time on plans you already trust.

workflow.plan_chunked.description: Enables chunked planning mode. Instead of running one long-lived planner task, GSD splits planning into a short outline task followed by several short per-plan tasks (roughly 3–5 minutes each). Each plan is committed individually, so a crash or interruption does not lose the entire planning session. This is especially helpful on Windows, where long-lived tasks can hang on stdio issues.

workflow.plan_drift_precheck.description: Runs a non-blocking codebase-drift check before `/gsd:plan-phase` spawns the planner. If your project's recorded structure (STRUCTURE.md) is stale — meaning directories, routes, or other structural elements have grown beyond `workflow.drift_threshold` — GSD shows an advisory pointing you to `/gsd:map-codebase`. It never blocks planning and never spawns the mapper automatically, so it is safe to leave on in autonomous and CI runs.

workflow.plan_review_convergence.description: Enables the automated plan→review→replan convergence loop in `/gsd-plan-review-convergence`. When enabled, GSD repeatedly runs plan-phase and an external AI review lane, feeding the review findings back into the planner, until the reviewers raise no further HIGH concerns (up to a bounded number of cycles). This replaces a manual back-and-forth with an automated loop. When disabled, the convergence command exits early with instructions to turn it on.

workflow.post_planning_gaps.description: Runs a post-planning gap report after all plans are generated (plan-phase step 13e). It scans REQUIREMENTS.md and CONTEXT.md decisions against every PLAN.md and prints a unified table showing which items are planned, missing, or only partially covered. This is non-blocking and purely informational — it helps you notice requirements that slipped through the cracks before execution starts.

workflow.research.description: When true, GSD runs a research agent before planning whenever research artifacts are missing or explicitly refreshed. The research agent gathers codebase and domain context so the planner starts from facts rather than assumptions. Keep this on unless you always want to skip the research step and plan directly.

workflow.research_before_questions.description: Makes GSD do a codebase research pass before it starts the interactive discussion questions for a phase. This gives the agent context so its questions are better targeted and less generic. It adds a little time to the discuss phase but usually yields a much sharper understanding of the work.

workflow.schema_drift_gate.description: Enables the drift gates that run after each execution wave. Two checks happen: a schema-drift gate that blocks verification if schema-relevant files changed but no database push command ran, and a codebase-drift gate that warns when structural additions exceed `workflow.drift_threshold`. Turn both off together only if drift detection routinely fires false positives on your project.

workflow.schema_push_detection.description: Enables ORM schema-push detection during planning. When GSD detects schema-relevant files (migrations, model definitions, ORM config) inside the phase scope, it injects a blocking push task into the plan so the database is migrated as part of execution rather than forgotten. Turn this off only if your project manages database schema entirely outside GSD's awareness.

workflow.security_asvs_level.description: Sets the OWASP ASVS (Application Security Verification Standard) level GSD uses for security review guidance. Level 1 is opportunistic and appropriate for most apps; Level 2 adds standard rigor for apps handling sensitive data; Level 3 is comprehensive and meant for high-assurance, regulated, or high-threat systems. The level scales both how aggressively the planner considers threats and how deeply the auditor verifies mitigations.

allowedValues.meaning: Level 1 — opportunistic. A lightweight security baseline suitable for most applications and internal tools.
Level 2 — standard. Adds systematic verification for apps that handle personal or business-sensitive data.
Level 3 — comprehensive. The deepest assurance level, intended for regulated, high-threat, or security-critical systems.

workflow.security_block_on.description: The minimum open threat severity that will block a phase from advancing. The auditor counts only open threats at or above this severity toward the blocking gate. Raising the bar to `"critical"` means only the most severe findings block progress, while lowering it to `"low"` makes the gate stricter. Set it to `"none"` to disable severity-based blocking entirely (threats are still tracked, they just never block).

allowedValues.meaning: Only critical-severity findings block advancement. Least strict severity gate — useful while triaging a large backlog of legacy findings.
High-severity and critical findings block advancement. The recommended default for most teams.
Medium, high, and critical findings block advancement. Stricter — adopted once a project wants to treat moderate risks as release blockers.
Low and above block advancement. Very strict — even minor findings must be resolved before the phase can advance.
Severity never blocks advancement. Threats are still tracked, but the gate is effectively disabled. Use when another process owns enforcement.

workflow.security_enforcement.description: Enables threat-model-anchored security verification through `/gsd-secure-phase`. When on, GSD runs security checks tied to your project's threat model before a phase can advance, using the ASVS level and severity gate configured by the other `workflow.security_*` keys. Turning this off disables security checks entirely — only do that for early prototypes or non-production experiments where security findings would be noise.

workflow.skip_discuss.description: Skips the discuss phase entirely, moving straight from planning to execution without the usual clarification step. This saves time on trivial or well-understood phases, but you lose the chance to catch misunderstandings early. Only turn this on when the phase's intent is already crystal clear.

workflow.smart_zone_tokens.description: Sets the token budget GSD uses to decide whether a phase is large enough to warrant splitting. When a phase's estimate exceeds this number, GSD recommends breaking it into smaller phases. It is an advisory policy default, not a hard limit, so the warning is a nudge to consider splitting rather than a blocker.

workflow.specless_probe_fallback.description: Controls what happens when a phase's SPEC is missing its Edge Coverage or Prosections sections. When on (the default), GSD runs a probing pass to discover those predicates and writes them into the plan. When off, the fallback is skipped and a visible marker is emitted so you know the probe was intentionally not run.

workflow.subagent_timeout.description: Sets the timeout in milliseconds for parallel subagent tasks such as codebase mapping. If a subagent takes longer than this, GSD stops it and reports a timeout. Increase this for very large codebases or slower models; the default of 300000 (5 minutes) fits most projects.

workflow.tdd_mode.description: Enables test-driven-development mode for eligible tasks. When on, the planner annotates qualifying tasks with `type:tdd`, and the executor enforces the RED/GREEN/REFRACTOR gate sequence: write a failing test first, make it pass, then refactor. Turn this on when you want TDD discipline applied automatically, and off when you want the planner to choose its own task types.

workflow.test_command.description: A custom shell command that GSD runs as the regression and test gate. When unset, GSD auto-detects the right command from your Makefile, package.json, Cargo.toml, go.mod, or pyproject.toml. Set this only when auto-detection picks the wrong command or you need special arguments for a one-shot test run.

workflow.test_gate_timeout.description: How long, in seconds, GSD lets the test runner run during the regression gate before aborting it. If tests are stuck in watch or dev mode instead of running once, the run is cut off with a warning. The default is 600 seconds (10 minutes); raise it for slow test suites or lower it to catch stuck runners sooner.

workflow.text_mode.description: Switches GSD's interactive prompts from structured AskUserQuestion menus to plain numbered text lists. This is primarily a compatibility and readability option for terminals or environments that cannot render the structured menus. Most users should leave this off.

workflow.ui_phase.description: Enables the UI design-contract gate during planning for frontend phases. When on, `/gsd-plan-phase` generates a UI-SPEC.md that captures the visual and interaction contract before implementation begins, so the UI has an agreed-upon design to build against. Turn it off for backend-only projects or phases that have no user interface.

workflow.ui_review.description: Enables the retrospective UI audit against implemented frontend code. When on, GSD runs a structured visual and behavioral audit of finished UI work against its UI-SPEC.md contract, catching layout, accessibility, and interaction drift. Turn it off if your project has no UI or you perform UI reviews through another tool.

workflow.ui_safety_gate.description: Blocks planning/execution when a UI-SPEC contract is unmet. Unlike `workflow.ui_phase` (which generates the spec), this key is the enforcement gate: when on, failing to satisfy the UI-SPEC.md prevents the phase from sealing. With both keys on, GSD generates the contract and enforces it — the intended default. Setting `ui_phase:true` and `ui_safety_gate:false` generates a spec in pipelines but does not block manual planning.

workflow.use_worktrees.description: Runs each parallel executor agent in its own isolated git worktree so concurrent edits do not collide. This is the safe way to get parallelism on a shared branch, but it adds overhead and can complicate merge handling. Turn it off to run sequentially on the main working tree, which is simpler and recommended for solo developers.

workflow.verifier.description: When true, GSD runs a verifier agent after execution to check that the phase's deliverables match its plan and acceptance criteria. It is one of the core quality gates that catches drift between what was planned and what was built. Keep it on unless you intentionally want no automated post-execution verification.

workflow.windows_enforce.description: Enables the blocking ship-pre gate for the broken-windows ledger (`.planning/WINDOWS.md`). When `true`, `/gsd-ship` blocks while the ledger has any open entry, forcing the team to disposition each tracked deviation before shipping. When `false` (the default), windows are still tracked — the executor and verifier populate the ledger — but ship does not block, letting teams adopt tracking first and enforce later.

workflow.worktree_skip_hooks.description: Lets executor commits inside worktrees bypass pre-commit hooks when they would otherwise fail or slow things down. By default hooks run on each task commit to catch issues early; this setting opts out of that behavior only where the project explicitly chooses to. Enable it only if your hooks are incompatible with the worktree workflow.
